title: PM DC motor loaded torque-speed equilibrium
description: Find the coupled electrical and mechanical operating point of a permanent-magnet DC motor with constant shaft load and viscous drag.
formula: V=RI+K omega; K I=Tload+b omega; omega=(K V-R Tload)/(K^2+R b)
assumptions: Steady forward motoring or stall; constant opposing load torque and linear viscous drag. No static-friction threshold is modeled.
motor_constant is both torque constant in N m/A and back-EMF constant in V s/rad, numerically equal in coherent SI units.
Permanent flux, fixed winding temperature, ideal brushes, no magnetic saturation, iron loss or commutation ripple. Check motor continuous/stall current and mechanical ratings separately.

references.title: Auburn University, Modeling Electrical-Mechanical Systems (DC Motors), slides 12-16
University of Ottawa, ELG4139 DC Drives, torque equation and steady torque-speed characteristics

constraints.message: Load torque must not exceed the applied-voltage stall torque in this forward-motoring model

title: Stepper microstep torque and static load deflection
description: Distinguish commanded microstep resolution from static positioning accuracy using the sinusoidal torque-angle law of a two-phase stepper.
formula: alpha=2 pi/S; delta_micro=alpha/m; Tinc=Th sin(pi/(2m)); delta_load=(4/S) asin(Tload/Th); stiffness=(S/4) sqrt((Th-Tload)(Th+Tload))
assumptions: Ideal two-phase sinusoidal torque-angle law with constant current-vector magnitude; four full steps per electrical cycle.
holding_torque is the peak torque at the same current-vector magnitude used during microstepping, not a mismatched two-phase-current nameplate value.
Static stable branch only, with load strictly below holding torque. Ignores detent torque, friction, harmonics, current quantization, elastic compliance and resonance.

Incremental torque is the torque immediately after one commanded microstep from an initially aligned unloaded rotor held fixed. It is not the torque change of an already loaded rotor and does not guarantee motion.

references.title: FAULHABER Application Note 015, Microstepping, equations 1-2 and Accuracy vs. resolution

inputs.label: Holding torque at operating current vector

outputs.label: Static mechanical lag behind commanded field
Local restoring stiffness at loaded equilibrium

constraints.message: The ideal two-phase model requires an integer number of electrical cycles, or a multiple of four full steps per revolution
Microsteps per full step must be an integer
Static load must remain strictly below holding torque for positive restoring stiffness
